finding: 858 brand names in the catalogue fold to the same key as another — case, an apostrophe style, an accent or a space. 2605 records sit on a non-dominant spelling of a brand the catalogue ALREADY holds under another name.
why_it_matters: brandFileFor() slugs the brand, so 'amul' and 'AMUL' land in different files, and /b/<slug>/ on the site shows a fraction of a brand's products. One appliances record is filed under the literal misspelling 'Llyod' — it is NOT a duplicate of anything in lloyd.jsonl (3 Star vs 2 Star, different model numbers), just a real product whose brand was typed wrong.
why_this_is_a_DECISION_not_a_fix: mintId hashes brand (schema.ts:183), and brandFileFor slugs it (schema.ts:187). Correcting a spelling therefore CHANGES THE RECORD'S ID and MOVES ITS FILE. Every crawler in this repo matches on the stored id — a session-long rule is 'never re-mint' — so a rename breaks the stable-identifier promise those crawlers depend on. It needs an owner's decision about identity, not a data pass.
what_is_NOT_safe: A looser edit-distance sweep returns 387 pairs, and most are DIFFERENT REAL BRANDS: Sugar/Sagar, Catch/Natch, Mango/Margo, Canon/CANOY, Kenstar/Yenstar. Auto-merging on similarity would destroy real products. Only the case/accent/apostrophe fold above is safe to treat as one brand, and even that should be reviewed.
